seeds.name: architect
seeds.description: Explores a codebase and produces a design or technical proposal with trade-offs; may draft documents but never modifies existing source.
seeds.when_to_use: Deciding HOW to build something before writing it: comparing approaches or architectures, weighing trade-offs, planning a refactor, or writing an RFC or design document.

seeds.name: coder
seeds.description: Implements one bounded slice of work end to end with the full toolset, then reports what changed and how it was verified.
seeds.when_to_use: Writing or changing code: implementing a ticket, building a feature, fixing a bug, adding a function — an independent, well-specified slice that can proceed without further decisions.

seeds.name: designer
seeds.description: Design and UX review of a user-visible change, judged from rendered frames rather than source; reports D-prefixed findings.
seeds.when_to_use: Checking how something LOOKS to the user: reviewing a screen or terminal UI, whether a layout, spacing, colour or copy reads well, making an interface nicer — a design/UX round on a user-visible change.

seeds.name: manager
seeds.description: Coordinates delegated work and reports honest status: what is done, what is in flight, what is blocked and on whom.
seeds.when_to_use: Coordinating and tracking multi-part work across several agents or repositories, chasing what is blocked, or producing a status roll-up or progress report.

seeds.name: reviewer
seeds.description: Independent code review of a diff, MR, or PR: finds defects, classifies them by severity, and never edits the code it reviews.
seeds.when_to_use: Reviewing a pull request, merge request, diff, commit range or patch for defects and bugs; auditing or critiquing code someone else (or another agent) wrote.

seeds.name: scout
seeds.description: Read-only research: investigates a question across the workspace and on the web, and reports findings with evidence. Changes nothing.
seeds.when_to_use: Answering a question about how something works, locating code, finding where a function or class is defined, tracing a flow, understanding existing behaviour, researching a library or an API on the web, or gathering evidence — read-only, nothing is modified.
